body.p: This Amendment responds to the Office Action mailed August 29, 2024. Claims 13-28 were pending in the Application prior to this amendment and claims 13, 14, 18- 26, and 28 were rejected. Claims 15-17 and 27 were objected to. Claims 14, 15, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27, and 28 are amended herein, and claims 13, 16, and 17 are cancelled. Accordingly, claims 14, 15, and 18-28 remain pending in the Application after this amendment.
Applicant thanks Examiner Jaime Figueroa for the courtesies extended to

Applicant's representative, David W. Dorton, during the telephone interview conducted January 28, 2025. During the interview, the rejection of claim 14 was discussed and the Examiner agreed that European Application No. EP 1 750 188 to Som et al. does not teach, or even suggest, the combination of features set forth in claim 14, as discussed more fully below. Applicant's representative also proposed amendments to the language of claims 13 and 18 to overcome the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §112. The claims have been amended herein in accordance with the telephone interview. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration in view of the interview, the amendments, and the following remarks.

FIGS. 1-3 were objected to for lacking descriptive text in certain boxes depicted in the drawings. FIGS. 1-3 have been amended herein to include descriptive text as requested by the Examiner. Support for the amendments to the drawings can be found
with reference to paragraphs 86 and 92-95 o the published Application (U.S. 2023/0173677). Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the objections to the drawings be withdrawn.

Claims 13-28 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) for informalities identified in claims 13 and 18. (Office Action at pp. 4-6.) The language of claim 13 (now incorporated into rewritten claims 14, 15, and 27) and the language of claim 18 has been amended as discussed during the telephone interview. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §112 be withdrawn.

Claims 13-28 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as allegedly anticipated by European Application No. EP 1 750 188 to Som et al. Claim 13 has been cancelled in favor of rewriting claim 14 in independent form. Applicant asserts that rewritten claim 14 is in condition for allowance because Som '188 fails to teach, or even suggest, the combination of method steps set forth in claim 14, including "the corresponding brake tests being carried out at individual different times and/or in individual different time intervals," as was discussed during the telephone interview. Rather, Som '188 contemplates that all brakes are tested at the same designated time or interval. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 14 be withdrawn.

Claims 18, 20, 22, 24, and 28 have been amended such that claims 18-26 and 28 each depend from rewritten claim 14. Applicant asserts that these claims are in condition for allowance for at least the reasons discussed above with respect to claim 14, and requests that the rejections of claims 18-26 and 28 also be withdrawn.

Claims 15-17 and 27 were objected to for depending from rejected base claims, but were indicated to be allowable if rewritten in independent form. Applicant thanks the Examiner for recognizing the allowable subject matter of these claims, and has rewritten claims 15 and 27 in independent form herein. Claim 15 has been further amended to include the subject matter of allowable claims 16 and 17 as alternative limitations in order to avoid fees for additional independent claims. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests early and favorable indication of allowance for claims 15 and 27.
In view of the telephone interview, and the amendments and remarks herein,

Applicant believes this application is in condition for allowance and respectfully requests allowance of the pending claims. If the Examiner believes any matter requires further discussion, the Examiner is respectfully asked to telephone the undersigned attorney so that the issue may be promptly resolved. The Examiner's prompt attention to this matter is appreciated.
Applicant does not believe that any fees are due in connection with this

submission, other than $690 for a two-month extension of time. However, if any additional fees are necessary to complete this communication, the Commissioner may consider this to be a request for such and charge any necessary fees to Deposit Account No. 60-1582.
